title: Staff Training for AI Medical Interpretation
summary: Train hospital staff to use an AI medical interpreter with role-based scenarios covering session start, interpreted communication, uncertainty.
body_markdown:
###


Training should teach staff to recognize language need, start interpretation, communicate effectively through the interpreter, respond to uncertainty, obtain human support when needed, and document the encounter.


###


Use role-based, scenario-based practice. Clinicians should practice real clinical conversations with numbers, medications, corrections, multiple speakers, uncertainty, and escalation instead of watching a software demonstration.


###


There is no universal training length. The better test is whether the staff member can complete the relevant workflow independently. Focus training time on realistic practice and a short skills check.


###


Human support can be used when the patient requests it, policy calls for it, another accessibility modality is needed, technology fails, or repeated clarification does not resolve a communication problem.


###


Track independent session starts, time to active interpretation, support requests, abandoned sessions, documentation completion, use by department and language, and reasons for human support.
